characterList.description: A middle-aged man with short, graying hair, wearing a light blue shirt with thin vertical stripes. He speaks off-camera and is not visible.
characterList.name: Interviewer

characterList.description: A middle-aged man with short, graying hair, wearing a light blue shirt with thin vertical stripes and a yellow lanyard.
characterList.name: Karl Holweger

content_metadata.description: An interview with Karl Holweger discussing the future of telephony in fundraising, recorded at the International Fundraising Congress in Holland on 22 October 2009.

qAndA.question: What color is the lanyard worn by Karl Holweger?

qAndA.answer: Save the Children's "ceasefire" campaign in Gaza.
qAndA.question: What specific example does Karl Holweger use to illustrate the effectiveness of SMS campaigns for donor acquisition?

qAndA.answer: Identifying "hand raisers" who express interest in the charity and following up with a telephone call to convert them into regular givers.
qAndA.question: What are the two steps in the "two-step approach" to donor acquisition?

qAndA.answer: He believes telephony will become the dominant communication channel for engaging donors and acquiring new monthly givers.
qAndA.question: What is Karl Holweger's prediction for the use of telephony by charities in the future?

qAndA.answer: Contrary to initial concerns, Karl Holweger suggests the TPS has actually made people more willing to receive phone calls from charities, as it has eliminated unwanted calls from commercial companies.
qAndA.question: How has the Telephone Preference Service (TPS) impacted telephony use by charities in the UK?

characterInteraction.description: The Interviewer poses questions, prompting Karl Holweger to share his insights and predictions about the fundraising landscape.

scenes.contextualRelevance: The interview highlights the evolving role of telephony in fundraising and the need for charities to adapt their strategies to engage donors effectively while respecting their preferences.

narrativeProgression.description: Karl Holweger discusses his predictions for the future of telephony in fundraising, focusing on the shift from cash gifts to monthly giving and the use of telephony for donor acquisition and stewardship.

scenes.thematicElements: Telephony in fundraising, monthly giving, donor acquisition, two-step approach, TPS, donor engagement, ethical fundraising practices.
scenes.title: Interview Scene

already starting to see that in the UK where the majority of Charities have supporter bases made up of regular monthly givers and most importantly they now tend to spend more money on the telephone
